name: Gyromechanic Gear
summary: In Kharanos, inventors seek Gyromechanic Gears for a bold experiment. They hope to reverse the mutations of leper gnomes.

sections.title: Components for Recombobulation
sections.body:
Radiation swept through Gnomeregan while gnomes fought to drive out the troggs. Many survivors became mad, irradiated leper gnomes. Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket will not abandon their twisted kin, so they have planned the Recombobulator. The machine is meant to undo radiation's effects.

Its prototype needs precise mechanisms that can bear the volatile pressure inside, including Gyromechanic Gears and Restabilization Cogs. Gnomeregan's fall ended local manufacturing. Now the inventors must salvage these delicate parts from hostile leper gnomes roaming Dun Morogh.

faq.q: What is a Gyromechanic Gear used for?
faq.answer: Razzle Sprysprocket in Kharanos needs Gyromechanic Gears as core parts for the Recombobulator. The prototype will use them with Restabilization Cogs in an attempt to cure irradiated leper gnomes.

faq.q: Where do these gears come from?
faq.answer: The gears are salvaged from Leper Gnomes outside Gnomeregan and from Gibblewilt in Dun Morogh.

faq.q: Can the Recombobulator actually cure leper gnomes?
faq.answer: Razzle Sprysprocket trusts Ozzie's schematics and believes changes to the combustion pistons and electrogum gel can restore their kin. The machine has not been tested against radiation poisoning on a wide scale.

faq.q: Why can't gnomes simply forge new gears?
faq.answer: Gnomeregan's fall shattered gnomish industry and put its finest tools, workshops, and automated foundries out of reach. Salvaging intact precision hardware around the city's edge is often faster than making parts by hand.

angles.text: As a gnome, each gear you salvage brings tinkerers closer to a chance to rescue their radioactive kin in the snows outside Gnomeregan.
As an engineer, you know the intricate design and tight tolerances of gnomish gyromechanic parts. They regulate unstable prototype machinery.
